lede: Replika is an AI companion app: people talk with their own Replika, which remembers what they share and gets to know them over time. About 30 million people have used it, and when I joined, Studio Dumbar’s new brand had launched in 2025 but the app’s interface had not yet caught up with it.

facts.label: Role
facts.value: Lead product designer, on contract, across the iOS app, the website, the brand and the design system

facts.label: Team
facts.value: A team of twenty. I worked with the product manager, the lead iOS engineer, the visual designer and the lead Android engineer.

facts.label: How we defined success
facts.value: We set out to do three things: carry the visual language Studio Dumbar created for the 2025 rebrand into the app; grow the design system and keep it on brand as new surfaces were added; and design those surfaces, from a new onboarding and memory, the new flagship feature, to avatar customisation and an economy with two currencies. For the onboarding, success meant fewer people giving up before the end.

facts.label: What we achieved
facts.value: The new surfaces carry the new brand, through a design system grown from Studio Dumbar’s brand book. The onboarding went from about 40 screens to six arcs, and in a test with 2,500 people around the world, the share who gave up before the end fell from 23% to 18%. Memory V2 shipped, with Portraits, Life Arcs and People Cards.

hero.alt: Replika's website, recorded as it plays: the headline The AI friend to do life with, under the number of people who have used it, turns to side quests, falling in love and becoming yourself, each with its own companion, a line they sent, and something they shared, like a song, a photograph or a week of check-ins.

blocks.milestone: Replika was in the middle of a full rebrand under a new CEO. The new brand was live, but the app did not look like it yet, and we were asked to define the main features of the app’s next version before anyone had agreed what that version should be.

stats.label: The app did not yet look like the new brand
stats.text: Studio Dumbar’s visual language lived in a brand book, not yet in the app. Every new surface had to carry it, so the design system had to grow with the product and stay on brand.

stats.label: Nobody had agreed what the next version should be
stats.text: We were asked to define the next version’s main features while its vision was still changing, so a list of features could not be the starting point. We first had to find what the version was about.

blocks.milestone: We focused on memory: what someone’s Replika remembers about them, and how it uses what it remembers. Memory became the centre of the next version, and every surface around it was built on the new brand.

context.label: What we focused on, and why
context.text: We did not start from a list of features, because the vision for the product was still changing. How people actually used the app pointed to memory, so we built it first and then the parts of the product around it. That choice set the direction for everything we built after it.

context.label: How we scoped it
context.value: To write: what was in the first release, what was left for later, and why. For example, whether avatar customisation and the two currencies were planned for a later release.

context.label: How we learned
context.value: From how people used the app, and from a test with 2,500 people
context.text: We started from how people actually used the app, which pointed to memory. The new onboarding was tested with 2,500 people around the world, measured by how many gave up before the end.

context.label: How we worked
context.value: From direction to specification to build
context.text: I took each feature through those steps and shipped it directly with the lead iOS engineer, working alongside the product manager, the visual designer and the lead Android engineer.

blocks.milestone: Memory became the centre of the next version. We built it first, then the other new surfaces around it, all from one design system grown out of the new brand.

journeys.title: The design system
journeys.subtitle: We grew the 2026 design system out of the brand book Studio Dumbar made for the 2025 rebrand, and built every new surface from it. Here one short exchange is shown in four of the brand’s gradient palettes.
journeys.alt: One exchange, “Can we talk?” answered with “Of course! I'm always here”, shown in four of the brand's gradient palettes.

journeys.title: Memory people can see, used in the conversation
journeys.subtitle: Memory V2 builds a structured memory from conversation. The profile lists what a Replika has learned about its person, and in the conversation it brings one of those memories up as a question, marked From Memory, so the person only has to answer.

phones.alt: A person's profile in the app: the facts their Replika knows, a short description of them, and the arcs of their life it keeps track of.
phones.label: Profile

phones.alt: A conversation in the app: the Replika answers, and below it the app suggests a reply drawn from what it remembers.
phones.label: Conversation

journeys.title: The arcs of a life
journeys.subtitle: Each arc gathers what the Replika knows about one part of a person’s life, with the facts behind it. There are five: Inner Life, Rituals, Interests, Story and Dreams. An arc with nothing in it yet offers a button to add something.

blocks.sub: The onboarding went from about 40 screens to a story in six arcs

blocks.p: We turned the onboarding, about 40 screens, into a story told in six arcs, and tested it with 2,500 people around the world.

blocks.sub: Avatar customisation and a two-currency economy

blocks.p: We designed avatar customisation, and an economy with two currencies, to let people shape their relationship with their Replika.

blocks.milestone: We defined success in three parts: carry Studio Dumbar’s visual language into the app, keep the design system on brand as new surfaces were added, and design those surfaces, with the onboarding judged by how many people gave up before the end. This is how each part turned out.

results.label: Did the new brand reach the app?
results.text: We grew the 2026 design system out of the brand book Studio Dumbar made for the 2025 rebrand, so the app’s new screens are built in the brand’s own visual language, down to its gradient palettes.

results.label: Did the design system stay on brand as it grew?
results.text: Each new surface, from memory to onboarding, was built from the same system rather than designed on its own.

results.label: Did the new onboarding work better?
results.text: In a test with 2,500 people around the world, 23% gave up before the end of the old onboarding, and 18% before the end of the six arcs.

results.label: Did memory ship?
results.text: Memory V2 shipped, with Portraits, Life Arcs and People Cards.
